statement: Convert a string s into a 32-bit signed integer, the way the C function atoi does.

First skip any leading spaces. Then an optional '+' or '−' sign sets the sign, positive if there is none. Then read digits until a non-digit character or the end of the string; leading zeros do not change the value, and if no digit is read the value is 0. Everything after that point is ignored.
Apply the sign. If the result is above 2³¹ − 1 return 2³¹ − 1, and if it is below −2³¹ return −2³¹. Otherwise return the result.

examples.explanation: The three spaces are skipped, the '−' makes the number negative, and the digits give 42.
Reading stops at the space after 4193, so the words are ignored.
−91283472332 is below −2³¹, so the result is clamped to −2147483648.

constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, ' ', '+', '-' and '.'
